registered.old: Apply waiver, prevention and disproportionate forfeiture where supported. Also ask whether there was an independent promise to produce the event, whose breach may support damages.
registered.new: Apply waiver and prevention where supported. A court may excuse a condition to avoid disproportionate forfeiture only if its occurrence was not a material part of the agreed exchange (Restatement § 229); that excuse does not cure a party's own uncured material failure, which may leave only restitution (Nelson). Also ask whether there was an independent promise to produce the event, whose breach may support damages.
registered.reason: § 229 lets a court excuse a condition to avoid disproportionate forfeiture 'unless its occurrence was a material part of the agreed exchange'; without that limit K-27 excused Kingston's security condition and gave Nelson's builder the full price (C&M 824, 830).
registered.reviewDepth: Relevant assigned casebook, supplement, selections and slide passages checked by two workers and the lead; not a full-opinion or subsequent-treatment certification.

registered.old: Jacob & Youngs treated the use of equivalent pipe as a minor departure in the circumstances. Substantial performance can satisfy a constructive condition while leaving damages for the defect.
registered.new: Jacob & Youngs treated an innocent, trivial use of equivalent pipe as substantial performance; a willful transgressor cannot claim the doctrine under Cardozo's opinion. Substantial performance satisfies a constructive condition while leaving damages for the defect; it does not satisfy a condition the parties made express by apt and certain words.
registered.reason: Cardozo: 'The willful transgressor must accept the penalty of his transgression' (C&M 850); the node let a builder who swapped pipe deliberately for profit reach 'Substantial'. Substantial performance satisfies a constructive condition only (C&M 851–852).

registered.new: Test the actual condition, and whether it is enforceable: courts in California, Nevada and New York refuse to enforce even a clear pay-if-paid clause as against public policy. In Luttinger no qualifying loan was available despite diligent efforts, and a proposed subsidy did not satisfy the specified financing term.
registered.reason: C&M 819 Note 2: California, Nevada and New York courts have invalidated pay-if-paid clauses as against public policy.

registered.old: A nonbreaching party may seek the value conferred when the other side materially breaches before completion. Algernon Blair permits reasonable value for accepted performance despite a losing bargain. Test any valid contract that still governs payment.
registered.new: A nonbreaching party may seek the value conferred when the other side materially breaches before completion. A party in breach may also have a claim: Nelson let a negligent builder who had not substantially performed recover the benefit conferred in excess of the owner's damages. Algernon Blair permits reasonable value for accepted performance despite a losing bargain. Test any valid contract that still governs payment.
registered.reason: Nelson let a negligent builder who had not substantially performed recover the benefit conferred less the owner's damages ($598.85, C&M 883–884); K-08 node e spoke only of a nonbreaching party, and node h cited Nelson for the contract remedy it denied.

registered.old: Kent was entitled to insist on Reading pipe even just because he preferred it; pipe that worked as well was not what he bargained for.

registered.reason: This is McLaughlin's dissent; Cardozo's majority held the innocent, trivial deviation did not forfeit the price (C&M 849–851).

registered.old: A builder who innocently used a different brand of equally good pipe did not forfeit payment for the house. Trivial departures are compensated in damages, measured by the drop in value when tearing out the work would cost far more than it is worth.

registered.old: First distinguish a condition from a promise about performance. Then ask whether the agreement is divisible, the condition was waived, or substantial performance applies. Compare those routes with Luttinger’s failed financing condition and Peacock’s ambiguous payment language.

Then ask whether the agreement is divisible, the condition was waived, or, for a constructive condition only, substantial performance applies. registered.old: A condition makes a duty depend on an event. Courts may interpret language, recognize waiver or apply substantial-performance rules to prevent disproportionate loss. registered.old: When a contract prices each item separately, a party can be paid for each item it fully delivered even though it did not finish the whole job. It gets nothing for items only partly carried out.
registered.new: When a contract sets a price for each unit of work, a party can be paid at that rate for every unit it fully delivered even though it did not finish the whole job. It gets no contract payment for a unit only partly carried out, such as a log driven halfway.
